beats.head: ONE PLATFORM, ANY MISSION
beats.body: The Generalized Marine Vessel Platform is one standardized core — hull, foils, powertrain, NavierOS — with a mission layer configured per use case. Foilborne-stable through Sea State 4. Hybrid-electric: ultra-long range under diesel-electric, switching to electric for low-signature operation.

beats.head: ASYMMETRIC BY DESIGN
beats.body: We do not build defense-specific vessels. We build standardized platforms for cargo, passengers, and defense on one base — the low cost structure our adversaries already enjoy, working for the United States and its allies.

beats.head: THE INDUSTRIAL GAP
beats.body: China produces over 1,700 ocean-going commercial vessels a year — more than half the global market. The United States produces fewer than five, holding 0.1% of global commercial shipbuilding capacity. A symmetrical contest of steel is unwinnable. Out-innovate, don't outnumber.

resilience_thesis.title: Global Resilience.
resilience_thesis.body: A standardized, energy-efficient platform for moving people and goods — built with allied nations through distributed manufacturing. In time of need, America has a maritime presence through vessels already operating around the world — deployable anywhere.
resilience_thesis.support_line: Commercial fleets are a strategic reserve: vessels built on this architecture are effectively pre-certified hardware. In times of conflict, capacity surges without waiting years for new keels to be laid.
resilience_thesis.placement: Opens the DUAL-USE beat — before sub_line and fine_print.
